data.why: matrix-editor opens TEICorpus XML collation files via a file-picker input (no server-side data loading); these are the repo's own tutorial example files, already aligned and ready to open, plus NeXML trees for the reconstruct-from-tree feature.

goals: Open a TEICorpus XML alignment of manuscript witnesses and inspect the matrix of aligned readings word by word
Mark and annotate variant readings across witnesses (e.g. tag scribal errors, omissions, or shared innovations) to build a critical apparatus
Export the edited alignment matrix for use in external phylogenetic tree-building software such as SplitsTree
Load a phylogenetic tree (NeXML) produced from the exported alignment back into the editor
Reconstruct the likely original (archetype) reading at each variation point using the tree topology (Fitch parsimony)
Produce a publishable critical apparatus/edition from the reconstructed text

review.summary: The tree states the interface's purpose exactly as the tutorial does: inspect and correct the alignment, export for tree-building, reconstruct by Fitch parsimony on a NeXML tree, and export an apparatus. The cited screens hold up. It needs small fixes before filing: move a few misplaced or bundled tasks, add the philologist's step of resolving {x, y} readings and saving the alignment, split the over-broad export and reconstruction features, and note the broken transliteration and that no export file was ever seen.
